name: Cocoa butter / shea / coconut oil
lead: Cocoa butter, shea butter and coconut oil are plant fats widely used in moisturizers, soaps and lotions, and are a traditional folk choice for trying to prevent stretch marks in pregnancy.[1][2][3]

A Wikipedia summary reports that a Cochrane review found no evidence that creams or oils prevent or reduce stretch marks in pregnancy.[4] A registered randomized trial of cocoa butter for stretch marks in pregnancy exists.[5]

paras: Cocoa butter is mostly triglycerides of palmitic, oleic and stearic acids and melts near body temperature; it is common in lotions and soaps for its emollient feel.[1] Shea butter is a triglyceride fat rich in stearic and oleic acids, used as an emollient and skin conditioner.[2] Coconut oil is about 82% saturated fat, mostly lauric acid, and is a raw material in soaps and surfactants.[3]

A registered randomized trial, "Cocoa Butter for Prevention of Stretch Marks" (200 participants, pregnancy, started 2004, completed), is listed on ClinicalTrials.gov.[5] Its results are not reproduced here. Broader reviews summarized on Wikipedia report no evidence that creams or oils prevent stretch marks.[4] No trials of shea butter or coconut oil for stretch marks were found.

lore.intro: These fats are mentioned as natural stretch mark prevention.[4]

quick.overview:
These plant fats are common moisturizing ingredients and a traditional choice for preventing stretch marks.

A registered trial of cocoa butter exists, but reviews summarized on Wikipedia report no evidence that creams or oils prevent stretch marks.
quick.mechanism: They act as emollients that soften and hydrate the skin surface; no mechanism for preventing stretch marks is established.
quick.risks: Sources reviewed describe no specific harms; individual skin reactions to any topical product are possible.
